rejected.title: Injury, concussion and safety
card: Concussion and knee injuries are common in sport. Concussion is a brain injury caused by a knock to the head or body. A common knee injury is a tear to the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL).
Rules and equipment
Rules, such as bans on high tackles, lower the chance of injury. Equipment, such as mouthguards and shin pads, helps protect the body. Neither removes the risk.
Return-to-play protocol
This is a set of steps that guides an injured athlete back to sport. It includes rest, a gradual return to activity and sign-off from a health professional.
A player with a suspected concussion should be removed from play at once. They should not return until they have followed the protocol.
rejected.remember: Rules and equipment lower the risk of injury, and a return-to-play protocol guides a safe return after it.

a.q: What is the main purpose of a return-to-play protocol after a concussion?
opts: To bring the athlete back step by step and safely
To prevent any other athlete from being concussed
To test whether the athlete is fit enough to be selected
To replace the need for rules and protective equipment
a.why: A protocol guides the athlete back through gradual steps, with health professional sign-off. It does not stop other players being injured, because that is the job of rules and equipment.
a.clue: Think about what happens after the injury has already occurred.

b.q: Jas, a netballer in Geelong, is hit in the head in a game and feels dizzy. What should her club do?
opts: Take her off and use the return-to-play steps
Let her rest for a quarter, then play on if she feels fine
Give her a mouthguard and send her back on
Move her to a position with less contact
b.why: A player with a suspected concussion should be removed from play and only return by following the protocol. A short rest is not enough, and a mouthguard is protective equipment that does not treat a brain injury.
b.clue: Which option follows the protocol rather than just reducing risk?

version.title: Injury, concussion and safety
card: Concussion and knee injuries are common in sport. Concussion is a brain injury from a knock to the head or a jolt to the body. A common knee injury is a tear of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL).
Rules and equipment
rules such as bans on high tackles, and gear such as mouthguards and padding, lower the risk of injury. Neither removes it.
A player with a suspected concussion should leave the game at once and not return that day, even if they feel fine.
Return-to-play protocol
a set of steps back to sport: rest, then a gradual increase in activity, moving on only without symptoms, and a doctor's clearance before full contact.
version.remember: Rules and gear lower the risk, and a step-by-step protocol guides a safe return after an injury.

a.q: Why does a return-to-play protocol build activity up in stages after a concussion?
opts: To check the athlete copes before the next step
To stop other players in the team being concussed
To keep the athlete fit enough to be picked again
To replace rules and protective gear in the sport
a.why: Each stage adds a little more activity, and the athlete moves on only without symptoms, with a doctor's clearance before full contact. Protecting other players is the job of rules and equipment, not the protocol.
a.clue: Think about what happens after the injury has occurred.

b.q: Kirra, a footballer in Ballarat, takes a hard knock to the head in the second quarter and feels dizzy. What should her coach do?
opts: Take her off and keep her out for the day
Rest her for a quarter, then let her play on
Fit a mouthguard and send her straight back
Move her to a spot with less body contact
b.why: A player with a suspected concussion should leave the game at once and not return that day. A short rest is tempting, but feeling fine later does not make it safe to go back on.
b.clue: A suspected concussion ends the player's game.

a.best: To check the athlete copes before the next step

b.best: Take her off and keep her out for the day
